question.text: A stop loss order is activated when:

answer.text: The last traded price reaches or crosses the trigger price specified in the order
The opening price matches the trigger price
The closing price matches the trigger price
The volume reaches a specified level

explanation.text: The Logic: A stop loss order remains inactive until the last traded price reaches or crosses the trigger price. Once triggered, it becomes either a market order or a limit order depending on the type specified. For a buy stop-loss, the trigger fires when last traded price reaches or exceeds the trigger; for a sell stop-loss, when it falls to or below the trigger. The Trap: The trigger is based on the LAST TRADED PRICE, not the opening or closing price. Note: Example - a sell stop loss with trigger 82.80 and limit 82.75 activates when price hits 82.80, then places a sell order at 82.75.
